Itqan

إتقان — daily tasks, habits and long-term goals in one calm place
Current stage: 4 · Updated 2026-10-31
86%70 of 81 tasks

Next actions

  1. New: setting a habit's time is simpler — one-tap quick picks (Friday: Thursday Maghrib to Friday Maghrib), From/Until with the days named, a 'Counts on' choice of the normal day with the Islamic day marked, and a picture of the window over day and night.
  2. Fixed: the 'Your data lives only in this browser' reminder no longer shows while sync is working — a sync counts as a backup.
  3. New: a habit can be tied to prayers or clock times — e.g. Friday between Asr and Maghrib, or Thursday's Asr to Friday's Maghrib, counted on the day you choose — with a countdown on Today. Settings → Day and prayers shows today's prayer times and how timed habits appear.
  4. New: Settings opens one section at a time — a side menu on the laptop, a list on the phone — so nothing is a long scroll away.
  5. New: Itqan now announces each update in a 'What's new' window when you open it (once per device); Settings → What's new lists them all. Also: a guide and checklist when you create a goal, and clearer on/off switches on notes.
  6. New: counted habits (pages, minutes…) show their totals in Insights → Amounts, against the previous period. Edit a counted habit to give it a full round — e.g. 604 pages and the page you're on — and it shows Round 1 · 250/604 and roughly when you'll finish; a finished round starts the next. Open Itqan on the iPhone once so it updates (data format v15); sync resumes after that.
  7. To do (owner): deploy the push relay once so browser installs (your friend's Edge on Windows) can send focus endings to a phone — run relay/deploy.sh, then set the repo variable PUSH_RELAY_URL (steps in relay/README.md).
  8. New: Notes (in the menu after Ideas, key 9). Type a line and press Enter to save a note, or start a checklist. Pin, colour and label notes, search them, archive the ones you're done with. Any note or checklist line can become a task. Projects and goals show their notes too, and in Ctrl+K, 'note: …' saves one. To keep a note on Today, open it and tap the sun; tap the sun on its card on Today to take it off. Open Itqan on the iPhone once so it updates (data format v14); sync resumes after that.
  9. New: streak savers. Every 500 XP earns one (you can hold 2); a missed day uses one by itself and your streak on Today survives. Tap the flame on Today to see your savers, the last four weeks and how it works. Your existing history counts, so you may already hold some.
  10. Reminders and check-ins with people now reach the iPhone as notifications, even with Itqan closed there (the laptop sends them, so it needs to be awake). Open Itqan on the iPhone from the Home Screen once so it updates (data format v12); sync resumes after that.
  11. If 'Alerts from my laptop' isn't on yet on the iPhone: Settings → Notifications → turn it on and allow once. The switches above it (focus endings, reminders, check-ins) choose what the phone gets.
  12. Insights has a new Focus section and compares every number with the previous period — pick 7, 14, 30 or 90 days at the top. Tap a bar on the phone to see its value.
  13. Focus can now be for a habit: pick it on Focus, or press the timer on a habit card. Finishing checks the habit in — its minutes for a minutes habit (e.g. "10 min"), otherwise one check.
  14. Training → Routines → Program now offers "Whenever I can" (no schedule). Fixed days and Rotation still work as before.
  15. Number keys: 7 Training, 8 Ideas, 9 Notes (Reminders no longer has a number key — use Ctrl+K or the menu).
  16. In Settings → Profile, pick your interface language (it follows you to your other devices). All four translations have had their independent review (S2-23); if a phrase still reads oddly, note it.
  17. Record this year's achievements so far; check the suggestions Itqan offers.

  • 2026-10-31S2-53 (ADR-045), from the owner trying to set up Surah al-Kahf (Thursday Maghrib to Friday Maghrib): the timed-habit editor was hard to follow — the day chips meant the day the window opens, then a separate 'which day does it count for?' question. Now the chips are the days it counts for (as stored, no conversion), and From/Until each pick a day relative to it (That day / The day before / The next day, named 'Thursday'/'Friday' when one day is picked) plus a prayer or clock time; the count day follows. The owner then added: the Islamic day starts at Maghrib, but a tick must land on one normal day of their choosing — so a window across two days shows 'Counts on: Thursday | Friday' under the picture (recount() keeps the window and moves the weekdays), the Islamic-day option tagged (opensInEvening()). Quick picks: Friday (Thu Maghrib → Fri Maghrib, sets Fri), Morning (Fajr → Sunrise), Evening (Asr → Maghrib), Night (Isha → Fajr next day). WindowPicture draws the window over the real day and night where the owner is (typical times without a location), dims outside it, marks opens/closes and the day it counts for, and redraws on every change. No data change. windowDays()/withDays() and the named list label ('Thu Maghrib – Fri Maghrib') tested. Checked in the browser at 1280 px and 375 px, English and Arabic (RTL).
  • 2026-10-30S2-52 (ADR-044), reported by the owner: 'Your data lives only in this browser' showed on every open although he syncs. The backup nudge predated sync and only counted downloaded backups; it started once his first task was 14 days old. backupNudge() in lib/backup.ts now takes the newer of the last download and the last successful sync; 'lives only here' only when there has been neither; sync broken for 14 days brings back 'It has been 2 weeks since your last backup'. 6 tests. Reproduced and checked in the browser with and without a recorded sync.

    • 2026-10-21S2-34, a day-boundary fix: a habit's history started on the UTC day of its creation, so a habit made between midnight and 03:00 here began the day before and counted that day as missed in its streak periods, rates and the weekly review.
